notes: Inbound from indie mobile/social game studio focused on lightweight real-time chat for synchronous multiplayer. Heard about Redwood from tweet; signed up for free credits 2026-02-20. Wants hosted API (self-serve) first, minimal infra ops. Primary concern: sub-200ms perceived latency for short chat replies and streaming partial responses to reduce perceived lag. Also high sensitivity to abuse/spam (open chat rooms) — need fast moderation hooks and rate limiting. Team is small, will likely start with single environment and expand to Dedicated if growth justifies it. Mentioned costs are tight: looking for predictable per-message costs + throttles.

requirements_summary: Workload: real-time chat for mobile/social game 'SquadStream'. Targets: p95 end-to-end response <200ms for short-turn replies; streaming preferred to show token-by-token text. Throughput: expect 200-400 concurrent chat actors at launch; spike to 1k for events. Cost sensitivity: wants guidance to keep cost per active user low (<$0.03/day initially). Moderation: immediate need for profanity/abuse detection (both sync and async), token redaction, per-user rate limits, IP/UID blocking. Model preferences: small/fast model variants, quantized where possible; fallback routing acceptable if latency spikes. Integration: JS SDK for client streaming + server-side relay.
product_fit_notes: Why Redwood: hosted API + streaming aligns with their self-serve path. Key asks map to Redwood features: streaming responses (lower perceived latency), routing policies (fall back to lower-cost variants), batching config to save cost on bursts, prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, token-level cost visibility in Console for ops. Security: audit logs requested; SSO deferred until later. SE recommended: start on hosted_api with low-latency model profile, enable request-level rate limits and moderation webhook to an async pipeline for heavy checks. Also suggested using lightweight client-side echo + server verify pattern to reduce roundtrips.
